object_description: hall wing with a two-storey front building, placed as a striking volume at the western edge
geometry_property: hall wing plus two-storey front building
striking volume at the plot edge
design_condition: the gymnasium volume is placed on the western edge of the plot so that a playground is created to the east together with the kindergarten, bordered by a playhouse and an orchard

positive: The building is divided into hall wing and a two-storey front building holding all other rooms
A playground is created to the east together with the kindergarten
It is bordered by a playhouse and an orchard towards the single-family houses
The white larch slats of the ventilated facade characterise the external appearance
Light colours and large window openings give the facade a friendly and atmospheric character
The simple skeleton construction gives good conditions for implementation as a wooden structure
Massive glued laminated timber beams enable a low overall structural height
The outdoor reference of the glazed room with counter is welcomed
The gallery is spacious and attractively laid out
The gymnasium and upper floor are well and conveniently organised and well lit
The open space concept takes overarching references into account and does justice to the small-scale structures
The outdoor design offers a high level of play value for different age groups
It appears balanced with and without a hard court
The planting with numerous fruit trees is differentiated and offers a variety of experiences
The project has a compact volume and a good cost-benefit ratio despite increased facade costs
Convincing due to the site setting, the organisation of the gymnasium wing and the small-scale outdoor structure
negative: The compatibility of the volumetrics on the outskirts is critically questioned
The facade details and roof connections are not sustainable for a wooden structure
The roof shape of the front building appears arbitrary
The canopy of the main entrance appears unbalanced
The entrance situation and access area are not managed overall on the ground floor
The staircases are unattractive and the spatial references are not harmonious
There is no direct connection to the hall, a disadvantage for sporting events
The glass content is relatively high
The approach fails architecturally through the incompletely convincing expression and facade detailing
The functionally superimposed entrance situation is judged a significant spatial defect
